name: Wheat
description:
One pound of dry wheat grain, sold by weight for food preparation or trade. It is not a mixed animal-feed ration or a prepared meal.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Preserves the official 1 cp per pound and actual grain mass; wrapping is negligible.

source.title: Devil's Table: Trade & Merchants
source.reference: SRD 5.1 p. 72: Wheat (1 lb): 1 cp; 1 lb. Original wording and custom-economy price/adjusted weight. See docs/CORE_CATALOGUE.md.

name: Flour
description:
One pound of ordinary milled flour in a simple wrapping, sold for cooking or commodity exchange. Water, fuel, baking work and finished bread are separate.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Preserves the official 2 cp per pound and dry flour mass; this is not a full sack at a one-pound price.

source.title: Devil's Table: Trade & Merchants

name: Cotton Cloth
description:
One square yard of plain cotton cloth. Its ordinary weave is suitable for domestic sewing and repairs, subject to the GM’s judgement about dimensions and strength. Thread and finished clothing are separate.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.
saleUnit: One square yard of cotton cloth

weight.notes: Source mass is unspecified; a square yard of plain light cloth weighs 0.25 lb. Project 5 cp deliberately sits between existing plain linen (4 cp) and heavy canvas (6 cp), rather than importing the SRD 5 sp price into a different textile economy.

source.title: Devil's Table: Trade & Merchants

name: Ginger
description:
One pound of dried ginger, sold as a named spice commodity. It can be portioned for cooking or traded; no medicinal or spellcasting benefit is implied.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Retains a full one-pound spice unit. Project 8 sp compares with 1 gp and remains dearer than ordinary grain and common domestic herbs.

name: Cinnamon
description:
One pound of dried cinnamon bark, sold for flavouring and trade. The wrapping contains only cinnamon; it is not a mixed spice parcel or a magical reagent package.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Retains the full one-pound source unit. Project 1 gp compares with 2 gp and distinguishes an imported culinary spice from cheap staple grain.

name: Pepper
description:
One pound of dried peppercorns in a tied wrapping. Grind or portion them as ordinary kitchen supplies; tools and prepared food are separate.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Retains the full one-pound source unit. Project 1 gp compares with 2 gp and matches cinnamon as an ordinary imported spice commodity.

name: Cloves
description:
One pound of dried cloves, sold by weight as a specialist spice. The GM determines regional availability; the parcel has no magical or automatic medicinal effect.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Retains the full one-pound source unit. Project 2 gp compares with 3 gp and sits above more common imported spices.

name: Silver Bar
description:
One pound of plain silver in a small trade bar. It is raw commodity metal, not coins, jewellery, powdered silver for a ritual, or a magical item. Purity and assay disputes are GM decisions.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Preserves the official 5 gp per pound and full metal mass. No conversion to coins or ritual material is automated.

source.title: Devil's Table: Trade & Merchants

name: Saffron
description:
One pound of dried saffron, packed as an expensive bulk spice commodity. This is a substantial trader’s parcel rather than a small cook’s pinch. Partial quantities and regional provenance are recorded manually.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Retains a full pound despite its unusually high value and volume. Project 12 gp compares with 15 gp; rare stock prevents the bulk parcel becoming a routine village staple.

source.title: Devil's Table: Trade & Merchants

name: Gold Bar
description:
One pound of plain gold in a trade bar. It is bullion rather than a collection of spendable coins. Exchange, assay and any manufacture are separate GM-adjudicated activities.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Preserves the official 50 gp per pound and full mass. It has no discount that would create a built-in coin/bullion profit loop.

source.title: Devil's Table: Trade & Merchants

name: Platinum Bar
description:
One pound of plain platinum in a trade bar, intended for high-value commodity exchange. It is not a stack of native platinum coins and is not converted into a wallet balance automatically.

One Item quantity represents the complete stated purchase unit. Stock quantity counts additional full units; any splitting, refining or processing is manual.

weight.notes: Preserves the official 500 gp per pound and full metal mass. Rare one-or-two-unit availability retains the high-value, low-volume role.
